subject: SIG: clarification on key rotation, retention, and HSM custody
messages:
From: Luke Harris <luke.harris@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>, Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM rotation and key retention

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the SIG submission. Our security team had a few follow-up questions specifically around encryption lifecycle and custody so we can close this section of the review:

1) Which KMS provider(s) do you use for the hosted Redwood API? Are customer data keys (CDKs) encrypted with a customer-managed CMK or a Redwood-managed CMK?
2) Do you use a hardware security module (HSM) for root key protection? Which vendor/managed service and where are HSMs located (region/cloud)?
3) Key rotation cadence for CMKs and DEKs (data-encryption keys). Are rotations automatic or manual? Do you have proof of rotation (logs/timestamps)?
4) Evidence request: redacted rotation logs, HSM custody attestations, and a sample CloudTrail/Audit entry showing key usage/rotation.
5) Retention policy for keys and key material after tenant termination — describe deletion/escrow schedule.
6) Any third-party access (support/backups) to unencrypted key material?

Preferred transfer method for artifacts is a secure share (SharePoint/Drive) or SFTP; please advise if you need an upload link.

Attached: acme-sig-questions.pdf (PDF with highlighted SIG items)

Appreciate a consolidated response and evidence package.

- Luke
Security Engineer, Acme Corp
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harris <luke.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM rotation and key retention

Hi Luke — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide the artifacts and a short write-up per question.

High-level answers to start:
- Hosted API: envelope encryption using AWS KMS for DEK wrapping; default CMK is Redwood-managed. Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt for BYOK (customer-managed CMKs).
- HSM: Root key material is protected in FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs operated by our cloud provider for hosted tier; Dedicated/Private can be configured with customer-managed HSMs.
- Rotation: DEKs rotate as part of automated rekeying (90-day cadence by default); CMKs have annual rotation where applicable. We maintain rotation proof in a dedicated audit bundle.
- Retention: Keys associated with a tenant are scheduled for deletion 30 days after contract termination; we keep redacted logs for 1 year per our retention policy.

I'll collect the redacted rotation logs and HSM attestations and share a secure bundle by next Wednesday (2028-06-21). Marcus — can you attach the rotation logs and the audit evidence we can share? Monica/Stephanie, please flag any PII that must be redacted before sharing.

Attachments: rotation-summary-2028-06.pdf (summary of controls, request timeline)

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM rotation and key retention (internal artifacts)

Naomi — sending the artifacts we can share after redaction. Summary below, full details in the attached bundle.

Quick technical details:
- KMS provider: AWS KMS (multi-region primary in us-east-1 with replicas in us-west-2 for DR). Hosted API uses envelope encryption: tenant DEKs are generated per-tenant and encrypted with our CMK; default CMK is Redwood-managed. Dedicated/Private customers may supply a BYOK CMK (AWS KMS or a wrapped HSM key).
- HSM: Root key protection uses AWS CloudHSM for root-wrapping keys (FIPS validated). For Dedicated we support vendor HSMs (Thales/Entrust) when customers provide an HSM endpoint.
- Rotation cadence: DEK rekey job runs daily for high-change volumes and enforces a 90-day rotation policy for long-lived data keys. CMK rotation is configured annually where supported; we store rotation timestamps and a signed rotation event.
- Logs: rotation events are logged to CloudTrail + an internal rotation ledger (signed entries). We have included a sample ledger extract and three rotation event entries (redacted).
- Key retention: On tenant termination we schedule deletion of DEKs and queue CMK-access revocation. Observable proof of key deletion is available (signed deletion event), retention logs retained for 1 year.
- Third-party access: No external vendor has access to plaintext DEKs in hosted mode. Support staff can request access to metadata only; any access requests are logged and require approval.

Attachments included (redacted): kek-rotation-logs.zip (redacted rotation ledgers, CSVs), redacted-hsm-audit.pdf (attestation excerpts)

Notes for Naomi: the kek-rotation-logs contain timestamps and signature hashes but do not include any key material. I recommend sharing the Drive link with Acme Security and noting items that were redacted.

- Marcus Lin
Head of Cryptography, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harris <luke.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM rotation and key retention — consolidated evidence bundle

Hi Luke / Acme team — apologies for the delay and thanks for your patience. Per our earlier commitment, please find a consolidated response and evidence package below.

Short answers (for SIG):
- KMS provider: AWS KMS (primary region us-east-1; DR us-west-2). Hosted-default CMK is Redwood-managed; Dedicated/Private support BYOK.
- HSM: Root keys are protected in AWS CloudHSM (FIPS validated). Dedicated/Private deployments can integrate customer HSMs (Thales/Entrust supported).
- Rotation: DEKs: automated rotation/rekeying, 90-day target cadence (daily rekey job for high-change workloads). CMKs: annual rotation where platform allows; signed rotation events are retained.
- Retention & deletion: DEKs queued for deletion 30 days post termination; signed deletion events provide proof. Logs retained per policy (redacted logs available for 1 year).
- Third-party access: No third-party access to plaintext key material in hosted deployments. Any support-level access to metadata is logged and requires approval.

Evidence bundle and transfer: I've uploaded a redacted evidence bundle to a secure Drive share (link below). Included items: redacted HSM audit excerpts, rotation ledger extracts, sample CloudTrail rotation entry, and a signed rotation summary. All artifacts have key material removed; hashes and signed events remain for verification. If Acme needs notarized attestation, we can coordinate SOC- or auditor-signed copies under NDA.

Attachments (in bundle): evidence-bundle-2028-06-21.zip, redacted-hsm-audit.pdf, kek-rotation-logs.zip
Secure link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3RedactedLink
Jira reference: SEC-842 (internal ticket)

If you prefer SFTP/SharePoint upload instead of Drive, let me know and I can have IT provision a one-time upload URL. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if any of the entries need additional context.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
